question: In an increasingly competitive market under pressure from cheap imports, European agri-food products must not only maintain high standards but also enjoy effective mechanisms which ensure their visibility and differentiation.
In the case of vulnerable agricultural regions, the promotion of products on the internal and external market can serve as a genuine means of economic consolidation and support for local added value.

The EU’s promotion programme received substantial funding for 2026, but actually accessing that funding remains a problem for many producers and organisations in peripheral areas or ones less well represented at an institutional level. Without a more inclusive approach, there is a risk that the funding available will always go to those who are already in a strong position.

Can the Commission state whether it will simplify and extend access to EU promotion programmes for agri-food products from vulnerable regions, including through dedicated criteria, enhanced technical assistance and better representation of small and medium-sized producers?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.6.2026) The Commission acknowledges the importance of simplifying and ensuring access to EU funding for promotion programmes for agri-food products from vulnerable regions.

The Commission has undertaken several initiatives to this end, such as publishing improved guidelines and frequently asked questions, and strengthening outreach, in particular by organising live-streamed info days in Brussels and encouraging similar initiatives in Member States.

The amendment to the relevant Delegated Act1 in 2024 removed the representativeness requirement through membership for agri-food sector bodies. The Commission is considering other changes soon that will further improve support for applicants.
These efforts aim to reduce the potential applicants’ concerns about burden and encourage participation from all Member States, including those that have historically been underrepresented.

The Commission is also considering measures to strengthen applicants’ ability in these Member States to design and deliver high-quality proposals, including technical support to improve understanding of relevant Union rules for programme development and implementation.

Additionally, the Commission recognises the need for better representation of small and medium-sized producers and is exploring ways to improve their access to promotion funding. These measures align with the EU's objectives of enhancing the competitiveness of the agricultural sector and supporting the economic development of vulnerable regions.
1 Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2025/70 of 21 November 2024 amending Delegated Regulation

(EU) 2015/1829 supplementing Regulation (EU) No 1144/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council on information provision and promotion measures concerning agricultural products: https://eurlex.europa.eu/eli/reg_del/2025/70/oj.
